newsitem.title: TANZANIA: More Zaireans flee to tranquil Tanzania.
newsitem.headline: More Zaireans flee to tranquil Tanzania.

text.p: Thousands of Zaireans are fleeing across a lake into Tanzania to escape fighting in the east of their homeland, aid officials said on Friday.

A spokesman for the U.N. refugee agency UNHCR in Tanzania said 8,600 arrivals had been registered in Tanzania since fighting began three weeks ago -- still a drop in the ocean in a conflict that has sent more than a million fleeing within Zaire.

The bulk of the arrivals in Tanzania are Zairean nationals made homeless by the fighting between government troops and ethnic Tutsi rebels, in an area which had for two years housed 1.2 million Rwandan and Burundian Hutus in refugee camps.
UNHCR Nairobi spokesman Peter Kessler said some of the refugees were Zairean soldiers and their families.
Local officials estimate another 5,000-10,000 refugees have arrived by boat in villages on the Tanzanian side of Lake Tanganyika but have not yet been registered.
Tanzania is already putting up more than 600,000 Hutu refugees who fled Rwanda after the 1994 genocide of up to a million people, mainly Tutsis, or fled Burundi's civil war.
A Tanzanian doctor told the national Guardian newspaper three refugees had died on arrival, two of them children suffering from anaemia and the third a woman who bled to death after childbirth.
